text:
Mitch Marner's second season in Vegas has gone exactly as his first suggested: a playmaker running a power play. He has 26 points in 22 games, 23 of them assists and 12 on the power play, and RotoBaller noted a 10-game home point streak in mid-November. Our numbers project him for around 89 points.

The odd part is the goals. He has 3 on chances worth about 6, and he's shooting under 6% against a usual 12 or 13 for a forward. That's a finishing slump, not a role problem, and it's the kind that ends. He has one goal in his last ten games while his chances have held steady.

The Golden Knights get 56% of the expected goals at five on five with him on, so the process is fine. The team around him is the worry: Vegas has dropped four straight, three of them past regulation, including both games against Dallas this week, where Marner went without a point. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had him in the 83rd percentile of forwards for primary shot assists last season, and that's what Ryan Craig is paying for. Watch the goals catch up to the passing.
headline: Marner is passing, not scoring, in Vegas
